chunks: From him, from Moalla, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Wallad al-Hannat, and Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is from the correctness of the conviction of the Muslim man that he does not please the people by angering Allah, and he does not blame them for what Allah did not give him, for sustenance is not brought by the greed of the greedy, nor is it repelled by the dislike of the disliking; and if one of you were to flee from his sustenance as he flees from death, his sustenance would overtake him just as death overtakes him. Then he said: Indeed, Allah, by His justice and fairness, made relief and comfort to be in conviction and contentment, and made worry and grief to be in doubt and anger.
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of correct conviction (yaqin) in a Muslim according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines the practical manifestation of *yaqin* (certainty) as maintaining divine pleasure over human approval, a core tenet of Shia ethical theology. It underscores that *rizq* (sustenance) is divinely decreed and inevitable, thereby linking spiritual tranquility to acceptance of God's will and identifying anxiety as a symptom of doubt (*shakk*). This narrative serves as a foundational text for understanding the psychological and spiritual dimensions of trust in God (*tawakkul*) within the Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Moalla, from Al Hassan Bin Ali A lWasha, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, 
and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, deom Abu Wallad Al Hannat, and Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It is from the correctness of the conviction, the personality of the Muslim that he does not please the people by Angering Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, and does not accuse them upon what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not Give him, for his sustenance is neither ushered by the greed not the greedy one, nor is it repelled by the dislike of the dislike; and if one of you were to flee from his sustenance just as he flees from the death, his sustenance would come across him just as he would come across the death’. 
Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, by His<sup>azwj</sup> Justice and His<sup>azwj</sup> Fairness Made the spirit and the rest to be in the conviction and the pleasure, and Made the worries and the grief to be in the doubt and the anger’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from him from Mu’alla from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Wallad al-Hannat and ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) once said, ‘It is due to a Muslim’s correctness of certainty that he does not make people happy to anger Allah and does not blame them for what (of belongings) Allah has not given him. The share of sustenance is something that is not driven by the greed of the greedy ones and is not pushed back due to the dislike of those who dislike. Even if one of you may run away from his share of sustenance just as one runs away from death, still his share of sustenance reaches him just as death one day will reach him.’ He then said, ‘Allah through His justice and fairness has placed in certainty spirit and comfort and agreement with the decision of Allah. He has placed anxiety and sadness in doubts and anger.’”
